summary: Meagher County, MT 50-ft pole L-4 lookout built 1937 on the Lewis and Clark NF; summer lookouts named 1938 and 1941; destroyed 1971 per firelookout.com; no site description found.

facts.design: 50-foot pole tower with L-4 cab; 1937 item describes four 50-foot log legs and a 14-foot square cabin
facts.status_note: firelookout.com says destroyed in 1971; the FFLA Montana list marks the tower gone

staffing.status: summer lookouts named in 1938 and 1941 newspaper items; no later staffing found

access.note: No source describes what remains at the site or whether visitors can reach it

events.note: A 1937 Big Timber Pioneer item, quoted by the Forest Lookouts page, says four such towers were finished or nearly so in the Little Belt Mountains, one on Williams Mountain; firelookout.com dates it to 1937
Arnold H. Chloupeck named as the summer lookout (The Independent Record, July 1938)
Bill Jones named as lookout (Billings Gazette, July 1941)
Lookouts on Williams Mountain and Porphyry Peak reported a fire near Black Butte, this side of Ringling (The Independent Record, August 1946)
National Geodetic Survey station record, marked as described by the Forest Service in 1964: a USFS lookout house on a tower
firelookout.com gives destruction in 1971; the FFLA list marks the tower gone without a date

evidence.supports: location 12 miles west of Neihart, Meagher County
1937 Forest Service placing lookout towers in the Lewis and Clark forest
evidence.quote: the forest service is now taking steps to place such stations

evidence.supports: 1937 towers finished or nearly so; one located on Williams Mountain
evidence.quote: Four towers have been completed or are nearing completion in the Lewis and Clark forest, all are in the little Belt mountains. One of these stations is located on Williams mountain

evidence.supports: four 50-foot log main supports for the towers
evidence.quote: Main supports for the towers are four 50-foot logs

evidence.supports: 14-foot square lookout cabin on the towers
evidence.quote: where the 14-foot square lookout cabin is mounted
Extending entirely around the outside of the cabin are 2-foot catwalks.

evidence.supports: 1938 summer work; Arnold H. Chloupeck to be lookout on Williams Mountain
evidence.quote: Joseph W. Nawrocki and Arnold H. Chloupeck have started work for the summer. Mr. Chloupeck will be lookout on Williams mountain.

evidence.supports: 1941 lookout Bill Jones; creosote on tower legs
evidence.quote: Lookout Bill Jones on Williams mountain had to bring in a quantity of creosote to coat the legs of his tower.

evidence.supports: 1941 flies in the cracks and woodpeckers drawn to the flies
evidence.quote: Flies were getting into the cracks and woodpeckers, seeking the flies

evidence.supports: 1946 fire reported by Williams Mountain and Porphyry Peak lookouts near Black Butte, this side of Ringling
evidence.quote: Lookouts at Williams mountain in the Tenderfoot district and at Porphyry peak on King's hill reported a fire this side of Ringling near Black Butte

evidence.supports: 1946 county crew sent out to fight the fire
evidence.quote: the county crew, supervised by Sheriff Mike Bergan, was taken out to fight it

evidence.supports: 1964 National Geodetic Survey station record: described by the Forest Service; lookout house on a tower
1964 station description: USFS lookout house on a tower
evidence.quote: STATION IS A USFS LOOKOUT HOUSE ON A TOWER IN T 13 N, R 6 E.

evidence.supports: FFLA Montana list marks the Williams Mountain tower gone

notes_for_editor: The 1971 destruction date rests on firelookout.com alone. The newspaper items are as quoted on the Forest Lookouts page; they were not checked against the original papers. No photo or current description found. The brief's 50-foot height and agency are confirmed. The 1937 Big Timber Pioneer item names the tower type only generally, so the L-4 cab comes from firelookout.com. The 1964 description is a National Geodetic Survey station record that says the Forest Service described the station that year.
